name: Show File Extensions
description: Stops File Explorer hiding the extension of known file types. Seeing '.exe' on a file that claims to be a PDF is one of the cheapest defences against disguised malware there is.

name: Show Hidden Files and Folders
description: Shows files and folders carrying the hidden attribute. Does not reveal protected operating-system files — that is a separate tweak.

name: Show Protected Operating System Files
description: Reveals system files such as pagefile.sys, hiberfil.sys and the boot folder. Useful when tracking down disk usage; keep in mind these files are hidden because deleting them breaks Windows.

name: Open File Explorer to This PC
description: Makes File Explorer open on This PC instead of Home/Quick Access, so a new window starts at your drives rather than a list of recent files.

name: Show Full Path in Title Bar
description: Puts the complete folder path in the File Explorer title bar and taskbar preview instead of just the folder name, which makes two windows on similarly-named folders tellable apart.

name: Stop Tracking Recently Opened Files
description: Stops Explorer's Home view from listing recently opened files. The history is what leaks 'what you were working on' to anyone who opens Explorer on your PC.

name: Hide Frequently Used Folders
description: Removes the frequent-folders section from Explorer's Home view, leaving only what you have pinned yourself.

name: Remove Microsoft Ads from File Explorer
description: Turns off 'sync provider notifications', the banner Explorer uses to advertise OneDrive and Microsoft 365 above your files. Genuine sync status icons are unaffected.

name: Enable Item Check Boxes
description: Shows a checkbox on each file when you hover over it, so multi-select works without holding Ctrl. Handy on a touchpad.

name: Disable Item Check Boxes
description: Removes the hover checkboxes from files and folders, going back to plain Ctrl-click multi-select.

name: Show Explorer Status Bar
description: Keeps the status bar at the bottom of File Explorer, which shows the item count and the size of the current selection.

name: Launch Folder Windows in a Separate Process
description: Gives each Explorer window its own process. Costs a little memory, but one hung window (a stalled network share, a bad shell extension) no longer takes the taskbar and desktop down with it.

name: Expand Navigation Pane to Current Folder
description: Keeps the left-hand tree in sync with the folder you are viewing, so you can always see where you are in the hierarchy.

name: Show All Folders in Navigation Pane
description: Adds Control Panel, Recycle Bin and your user folder to the Explorer navigation pane, matching the classic Windows tree.

name: Disable Thumbnail Caching
description: Stops Windows writing thumbs.db-style caches for image and video folders. Thumbnails still show, they are just regenerated each visit — slower browsing, but no cached previews of files you have since deleted.

name: Show Icons Instead of Thumbnails
description: Draws generic file-type icons rather than rendering a preview of every image and video. Makes large media folders open instantly at the cost of not seeing what is in them.

name: Disable AutoRun on All Drives
description: Blocks AutoRun and AutoPlay on every drive type, including USB sticks and optical media. This is the setting that stops a plugged-in drive from executing anything on its own.

name: Ignore autorun.inf Files
description: Tells Windows to treat every autorun.inf as if it were empty, which is the belt-and-braces companion to disabling AutoRun itself.

name: Clear Recent Documents on Sign Out
description: Empties the Recent Items list every time you sign out, so the trail of what you opened does not survive the session.

name: Restore Folder Windows at Sign In
description: Reopens the Explorer windows you had open when you signed out. Convenient, though it does redisplay your working folders to anyone who signs in as you.

name: Hide Drives With No Media
description: Hides empty card readers and optical drives from This PC, so the drive list only shows things you can actually open.

name: Show Drives With No Media
description: Keeps empty card readers and optical drives visible in This PC, which is what you want when you are diagnosing whether a reader is detected at all.

name: Disable the Sharing Wizard
description: Replaces the simplified sharing wizard with the classic Advanced Sharing dialog, which exposes the real share and NTFS permissions instead of guessing at them.

name: Remove '- Shortcut' Suffix From New Shortcuts
description: Stops Windows appending '- Shortcut' to the name of every shortcut you create. Existing shortcuts keep their current names.

name: Disable Pop-up Description Tooltips
description: Stops the yellow pop-up description box appearing when you hover over a file or folder.

name: Disable Folder Size in Tooltips
description: Stops Explorer walking an entire folder tree to total up its size for a tooltip. Noticeably faster on folders with tens of thousands of files.

name: Disable Colour for Compressed and Encrypted Files
description: Stops Explorer showing NTFS-compressed files in blue and encrypted files in green, for a plainer file list.

name: Restore the Full Right-Click Menu (Windows 11)
description: Brings back the complete Windows 10 context menu, so 'Show more options' is no longer needed to reach entries added by 7-Zip, Git, Notepad++ and the rest. File Explorer restarts to apply.

name: Disable File Explorer Search History
description: Stops Explorer remembering and suggesting your previous search terms in the search box.

name: Disable 'Find Devices and Content' Prompt
description: Suppresses the network discovery banner Explorer shows the first time you open Network on a new connection.

name: Keep the Explorer Ribbon Expanded
description: Pins the Windows 10 File Explorer ribbon open instead of collapsing it after each command.

name: Delete Without the Confirmation Dialog
description: Sends files straight to the Recycle Bin with no 'are you sure' prompt. The Recycle Bin still holds them, so this is undo-able — unless you also empty it.

name: Always Confirm Before Deleting
description: Restores the 'Are you sure you want to move this to the Recycle Bin?' prompt for file deletions.

name: Show Seconds on the Taskbar Clock
description: Adds seconds to the system tray clock. Costs a small amount of extra redraw work each second, which matters only on very low-power hardware.

name: Hide Libraries From the Navigation Pane
description: Removes the Libraries node from the Explorer tree for users who navigate by real folders instead.

name: Sort File Names Literally, Not Numerically
description: Sorts 'file10' before 'file9', the way a plain string comparison would. Turn this on if you rely on zero-padded names and find Windows' number-aware sorting surprising.

name: Stop Blocking Files Downloaded From the Internet
description: Stops Windows attaching a 'mark of the web' zone tag to downloaded files, which removes the 'This file came from another computer' unblock prompt. This also removes a real safety net — SmartScreen and Office Protected View both rely on that tag.

name: Keep Marking Files Downloaded From the Internet
description: Restores the mark-of-the-web tag on downloaded files, so SmartScreen and Office Protected View can tell local files from ones that arrived over the internet.

name: Disable OneDrive Files On-Demand Placeholders
description: Stops Explorer showing cloud-only placeholder files that download when opened. Everything OneDrive syncs then has to be kept fully on disk.

name: Exclude the Gallery From Indexing
description: Stops the Windows 11 Explorer Gallery view from asking the search indexer to catalogue every photo on the machine, which is what makes the indexer churn after a large photo import.

name: Hide Cloud Files From Explorer Home
description: Stops File Explorer's Home view pulling recommended documents out of the OneDrive and Office account signed in on this PC.
